subject: FinServe discovery — Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finserve.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinServe discovery — Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex — great to meet you and Priya earlier. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned.

TL;DR: primary goal is to reduce inference unit cost while meeting sub-200ms p95 latency for customer-facing chat flows. We believe a combination of batching, prefix caching, and a quantized model variant can materially reduce token spend and monthly TCO.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-user cost on prod due to long context windows and high QPS from search+chat flows.
- Inconsistent latency when traffic spikes (affects SLAs to business lines).
- Security/compliance needs for audit logs and customer data retention policies.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Validate a TCO estimate for your 2 production routes (chat support, document search) at current QPS and at +3x growth.
2) Identify concrete levers we can apply: batching, KV/prefix caching, model quantization, and routing to cheaper variants for non-latency-critical jobs.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team next week to validate assumptions and run a small pilot.

High-level TCO notes (back-of-envelope from our call):
- Current estimated token spend: ~12B tokens/month.
- With continuous batching + prefix caching we typically see 20–40% token reduction on search/chat workloads with repeating prefixes.
- Quantized model variant + optimized kernels can reduce GPU cost per token by ~30% for production mixes we’ve seen at FinServe scale.
- Combined, a plausible 40–55% reduction in monthly inference cost vs current baseline (we’ll validate in the workbook).

Attached: FinServe_TCO_model_v3.xlsx (TCO workbook) and redwood_product_specs.pdf (deploy/variant options). The workbook includes: current baseline, assumptions, sensitivity to QPS/context length, and recommended configuration for pilot.

Recommended next steps:
1) You review the TCO workbook — I’ve filled the baseline with the numbers you gave during the call.
2) Rafael (SE) and Dev (SRE/infra) join a 60-minute technical deep-dive to validate cacheability patterns and confirm feasibility of the quantized variant — propose Fri 7/17 10:00am PT.
3) If validated, we’ll stand up a 2-week pilot (dedicated capacity) using 1 reserved pool + prefix cache; milestone: measured p95 latency and realized token savings.

Is Friday 7/17 10:00am PT good for the deep-dive? Happy to move it if you have conflicts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: FinServe_TCO_model_v3.xlsx (Excel, 180KB)
Attachment: redwood_product_specs.pdf (PDF, 340KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finserve.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 18:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FinServe discovery — Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — helpful summary and appreciated the quick follow-up. A few quick clarifications:

- The 12B token figure is for inference-only (we’ll confirm with infra if logging/monitoring adds more).
- Our peak p95 latency SLA target is 250ms across west/us-east; sub-200ms would be ideal for prioritised routes.
- Security: we need KMS integration and per-request audit logs for a subset of enterprise customers — can Rafael/Dev confirm both are standard options?

Fri 7/17 10:00am PT works for our team. I’ll block it and send a calendar invite with an agenda. We’d like the workbook by EOD tomorrow so our FinServe finance manager can review before the call.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations | FinServe
alex.johnson@finserve.com | +1 (212) 555-0114

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finserve.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finserve.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinServe discovery — Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex — quick notes from the SE side:
- KMS/HSM integrations are supported (we’ll share the KMS integration doc in the drive link). Per-request audit logging is supported; we’ll surface retention and export options in the deep-dive.
- About caching: to realize the 20–40% savings we referenced, we’d enable: 1) prefix caching for chat templates and repeated user prompts, and 2) KV cache for doc search session state. We’ll bring sample telemetry dashboards to show expected hit rates.
- Quantized variant: we’ll propose a 16-bit -> 8-bit quantized model for the pilot; performance/regression testing is part of the validation plan.

I’ll prep the technical checklist and a short runbook for the pilot.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Marissa
